At a glance: We are bearish through Fri 13 Nov, 8:15 AM ET.

We await 1.11010–1.11080; invalidation is 1.11390.

We assign Main 50% and the alternative 35%.

EUR/USD: bearish at 1.1101–1.1108, wrong above 1.1139: 4h chart of Euro / US dollar spot (ICE). Chart: TradingView. Plan levels: Capital Chronicle.
What is priced in

We see EUR/USD down 0.74% on 11 Nov after a 0.48% decline on 10 Nov. We read about 91% pricing for a December rate increase as evidence that a hike was already widely expected.

We see the 10 Nov close of 1.11688 below the 20-day average at 1.11905. We also see it below the 50-day average at 1.12711 and the 200-day average at 1.15007.

We cannot quantify the expected price swing or compare option prices because those observations were absent. That limits our view of how much further the repricing can run.

Positioning

We see speculative euro positions net short by 18% of outstanding contracts as of 3 Nov. We regard that concentration as a warning that short sellers could close their positions after the sharp decline.

We also see buyers from the 9 Nov rally above 1.1200 caught by the subsequent decline.

We do not know where these traders entered. Their exposure can amplify a rebound without proving that one has begun.

Fear

We cannot assess fear in options because expected price swings and the relative pricing of bullish and bearish options were unavailable.

The crowded short trade describes vulnerability to a rebound. It does not measure whether option buyers are paying for protection.

Structure

We anchor the entry area at 1.11010–1.11080, spanning the broken 1.11044 support from 29 Oct. We place this area beneath the 14 and 28 Oct daily lows at 1.11129.

We see the break as significant because 1.11044 was the lowest daily low across the 300 available sessions. We see 1.10867 below the former 1.11044–1.12731 range.

We therefore require a return to the broken floor before expressing the view. A lower quote alone does not supply that entry.

The story

We connect the break below 1.11044 to the hot October inflation release and renewed expectations of higher interest rates.

We have moved the bearish entry area because the earlier areas now sit above the 1.11390 invalidation level. We retain caution because the supplied odds do not establish a measured advantage.

We distinguish the new break from the older selling pressure. The entry shifts with that change.

Macro

We attribute the decline mainly to expectations of higher US rates while the European Central Bank remains on hold. Our comparison uses US two-year yields of 4.51% on 6 Nov and euro-area yields of 2.958% on 5 Nov.

We use these earlier readings because yields after the inflation release were unavailable. We also retain European Central Bank warnings about inflation risks as a counterweight to the dollar’s strength.

We compare the earlier yields as a dated backdrop, not proof of the spread after inflation.

The scenarios

We give Main 50%: EUR/USD reaches 1.10400 or lower before 1.11390 or higher by Fri 13 Nov, 8:15 AM ET. We treat 1.10400 as a projection because the available price history provides no established support below the broken floor.

We give the alternative 35%: short sellers closing positions lift EUR/USD above 1.11390 before it reaches 1.10400. We see European Central Bank inflation warnings and the 13 Nov euro-area growth release as possible support for that rebound.

The plan

We remain bearish and await 1.11010–1.11080, with entry at 1.11035 and invalidation at 1.11390. We keep the entry window open through Thu 12 Nov, 4:00 PM ET.

We keep the plan’s horizon at Fri 13 Nov, 8:15 AM ET. We wait for the return because selling near the low adds to an already crowded bearish position.

What would change our mind

We cancel the entry idea if a completed 15-minute period records a high at or above 1.11390.

We reject the bearish thesis after a daily close above 1.11390 or official US two-year yields below 4.51% on 12 Nov. We place 1.11390 above the hourly lows at 1.11362–1.11372 and the 30 Oct daily low of 1.11365.

How this view was built: a main case, a written case against it, then a final decision. The plan was fixed at Wed 11 Nov, 11:19 AM ET, before this page was published.

Current entry status is unavailable (updated Wed 11 Nov, 11:20 AM ET).
